catalog_quote: In Bidayuh the ultima (last syllable) is the nucleus of the word. It receives the peak of word stress—at least in citation forms (words that are pronounced individually). ... In some words of the shape (C)V.V(C), in western dialects (Singai, Jagoi) and also in Rara, the same vowel occurs in both the ultima (last syllable) and the penult (second-to-last syllable). In such words initiation of stress (accent) on the ultima vowel is usually perceptible: (C)V1.ˈV1(C). [Part II p.47] ... Because word stress falls on the final syllable in Bidayuh citation forms, and perhaps in context, a clitic receives the stress placement in the word to which it is attached. [Part II fn.79, p.94] ... an accentual difference is not evident in the contemporary Land Dayak languages. They consistently accent the final syllable of the stem; this is especially evident in utterance-final position. [Part III p.292] …

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable (ultima) of the word/stem, at least in citation forms and most clearly utterance-finally; Rara is explicitly included (ultima stress audible even in V1.V1 rearticulated-vowel words). Corroborated language-specifically by Sudarsono 2013 (snippet): 'Word stress in Bakatik generally falls on the word-final syllable. Thus, it is not phonemic.'
new_statements.exceptions: Part II fn.79 (p.94): because stress is word-final in citation forms, an attached (post-)clitic receives the stress of the word it attaches to. No lexical exceptions mentioned. Sudarsono 2013 says 'generally' word-final without listing exceptions (snippet only).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms / words pronounced in isolation (Part II); 'final syllable of the stem... especially evident in utterance-final position' (Part III). The general statements are framed for 'Bidayuh' (a study whose corpus includes the Rara wordlists) and for 'the contemporary Land Dayak languages'; the Rara-specific sentence concerns (C)V.V(C) words. Stress is described as non-contrastive.
new_statements.identity_note: Rensch et al. 2012's 'Rara' data are the Sarawak Rara Bakati' of Lundu District (kampungs Kendaie and Pasir Ilir), supplemented by Carmen Bryant's West Kalimantan Lara' list = Glottolog rara1235 / ISO lra. The general stress sentences are framed for 'Bidayuh' (whose study corpus includes Rara) and for 'the contemporary Land Dayak languages' (land1261); the sentence naming Rara concerns (C)V.V(C) words. Sudarsono's 'Bakatik' (2002/2010/2013) is the whole language comprising Lara (= Rara, rara1235), Sara and Riuk (= Sara Bakati', sara1341) dialects; which dialect his phonology rests on could not be determined from snippets (his inventory includes /ə/, which Rensch says Rara lacks). Azharie et al. 2001 'bahasa Bakatik' is explicitly the speech of 'suku Dayak Lara' (Rara) in Kec. Bengkayang, Ledo, Sanggau Ledo and Seluas.
